title: Good to know: case-opening
statement: A social worker can talk with your child at school without a court order, as long as no police officer is there. They must tell you afterward.
source_name: California Courts Self-Help Guide, "What to do if your child is removed"; Penal Code 11174.3
source_says: The social worker does not need a court order to talk to your child at school, as long as there is not a police officer present
steps: Grep found the after text at stageDepth.ts line 22. Searched "Penal Code 11174.3 interviewed during school hours", opened the Justia page for 11174.3: it says a suspected victim "may be interviewed during school hours, on school premises" and says nothing about parents, police or court orders. Then opened the Self-Help Guide page for parents, which has all three points. Its next sentence reads: "After the social worker talks to your child at school, they have to tell you that they interviewed your child at school." Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Good to know: eighteen-month
statement: If you are 16 or older, you should have a written plan for adult life. Ask to see it.
source_says: for a child who is 16 years of age or older ... the case plan shall include the transitional independent living plan (TILP), a written description of the programs and services
steps: Grep found the after text at line 205. Searched "WIC 16501.1 transitional independent living plan 16 years", opened the public.law page for 16501.1 and read (g)(16)(A)(ii). The sentence opens with "When appropriate". Paragraph (g)(13)(A) says a child 12 or older in a permanent placement can review, sign and "receive a copy of the case plan", which supports "Ask to see it". Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

steps: Grep found the after text at Timeline.tsx line 72. title: Timeline detention yourRights
statement: Right to ask for visits with your child. The judge can limit them.
source_name: Cal. Rules of Court, rule 5.670(c)(1); California Courts Self-Help Guide for parents
source_says: determine if contact pending the jurisdiction hearing would be beneficial or detrimental to the child, and make appropriate orders.
steps: Grep found the after text at line 86. Searched "rule 5.670 initial hearing detention visitation", opened rule 5.670 on courts.ca.gov and read (c)(1): "The court must consider the issue of visitation between the child and other persons". Opened the Self-Help Guide for parents: "When your child is removed, you can also ask the social worker to set up frequent visits with your child." Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Timeline disposition yourRights
statement: Right to visits as often as is safe and good for your child
source_says: any order placing a child in foster care, and ordering reunification services, shall provide ... Visitation shall be as frequent as possible, consistent with the well-being of the child.
steps: Grep found the after text at line 162. Searched "WIC 362.1 visitation shall be as frequent as possible", opened the public.law page for 362.1. The frequency and safety words match the chip ((B): "No visitation order shall jeopardize the safety of the child."). But the opening of (a) ties the rule to an order that places the child in foster care and orders reunification services. The chip states the right with no condition. The card around the chip is about a case plan with services, so the reader may already be in that group. Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.
fix: If the judge orders services to get your child back, you have a right to visits as often as is safe and good for your child.

title: Timeline disposition yourRights
statement: You can ask the social worker for the visit schedule in writing
source_says: the frequency of contact between the natural parents or legal guardians and the child shall be specified in the case plan.
steps: Grep found the after text at line 187. Opened the public.law page for 16501.1. (g)(5)(A) puts contact frequency in the written case plan. (g)(9)(B) says sibling visit schedule information "shall be provided to the child's out-of-home caregiver as soon as possible after the court order is made". (k) says "The child's caregiver shall be provided a copy of a plan outlining the child's needs and services." The chip only says the caregiver can ask. Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Timeline eighteen-month yourRights
statement: You can ask to be considered for guardianship or adoption
source_name: WIC 366.26(k)(1), (b)(3); Judicial Council caregivers booklet
source_says: the application of any person who, as a relative caretaker or foster parent, has cared for a dependent child ... shall be given preference
steps: Grep found the after text at line 304. Opened the public.law page for 366.26. (k)(1) gives a caretaker's adoption application preference when the agency finds strong emotional ties. (b)(3) lets the court "Appoint a relative or relatives with whom the child is currently residing as legal guardian". The caregivers booklet says "If adoption is the permanent plan and you would like to adopt the child, the attorney from the Department of Social Services will usually present that information to the court." The chip only says the caregiver can ask. Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Dashboard What matters: eighteen-month
statement: Finish everything left on your case plan. For most parents this is the last deadline. Ask your lawyer if more time is possible for you.
source_says: the court may continue the case for up to six months for a subsequent permanency review hearing, provided that the hearing shall occur within 24 months
steps: Grep found the after text at line 87. Searched "WIC 366.22 permanency review hearing 24 months", opened the public.law page. (a)(3): "Unless the conditions in subdivision (b) are met" and the child is not returned, "the court shall order that a hearing be held pursuant to Section 366.26." (b)(1) lists who can get more time: a parent making progress in court-ordered residential drug treatment, a minor or nonminor dependent parent, or a parent recently out of jail, an institution or immigration custody. Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Onboarding
statement: If you cannot pay, ask the judge at your first hearing. The judge will give you one.
source_says: and the child has been placed in out-of-home care, or the petitioning agency is recommending that the child be placed in out-of-home care, the court shall appoint counsel
steps: Grep found the after text at line 678. The code shows this sentence to the parent role only. Searched "WIC 317 appoint counsel parent financially unable", opened the public.law page. (b) is quoted: the judge must appoint when the child is out of the home or the county asks for that. (a)(1) covers other cases: "the court may appoint counsel as provided in this section." (d): counsel acts "at the detention hearing" and after. The court guides drop the condition but are written for removal cases: the Self-Help Guide page titled "What to do if your child is removed" says "If you cannot afford a lawyer, the judge will assign one to you." and the booklet says "The first time you go to court, the judge will give you a lawyer, if you can't afford one." Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.
fix: If you cannot pay, ask the judge at your first hearing. If your child was removed, or the county wants to remove your child, the judge must give you one. In other cases the judge can give you one.

title: Onboarding
statement: Your answers are private. We do not share them with CPS or the court.
source_name: Anchor Privacy Policy, last updated November 2026 (src/screens/PrivacyPolicy.tsx)
source_says: We do not share your personal information with courts, child welfare agencies, or any government entity.
steps: Grep found the after text at line 1008. This is a promise about the app itself, so the only source is the app's own privacy policy. Read src/screens/PrivacyPolicy.tsx: the quoted words match, and it also says "We do not share it with courts, social workers, or government agencies." Limits of this check: the policy says Preparation Guide text goes to an AI service and that Supabase and Vercel hold data; it says nothing about subpoenas or court orders for data; I saw onboarding write to Supabase but did not audit where data goes after that. Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

title: Under 13 page
statement: There is also a state office that helps kids in foster care when something is wrong. It is called the Foster Care Ombudsperson. You can call them. The call is free.
source_name: California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson website
source_says: The California Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson ... toll free hotline at 877-846-1602 ... Our office was created to serve foster youth.
steps: Grep found the after text at line 37. Searched "California Foster Care Ombudsperson toll-free", opened fosteryouthhelp.ca.gov and its contact page. The site is marked "Official website of the State of California". The office looks into complaints about "foster youth rights, care, placement, and services". Contact page hours: Monday to Friday, 8AM to 5PM. Full name is "Office of the Foster Care Ombudsperson". Pages were read through the web fetch tool, which returns short quoted segments.

For "private", opened unitedwaysca.org/get-help: "211 is a free, confidential, 24-hour service that helps people find local resources in times of need."
